title.narrative: Lighting an African Family (LAAF) Project: Improving access to Clean Energy and environmental practices in Africa

description.narrative:
According to the World Bank, 2023, roughly half of the continent’s population still lack access to electricity, this has gone up in recent years due to population growth outpacing new connections, especially in African urban areas. In places where connection exists, there are challenges of supply inconsistencies and frequent black outs. This stifles industrial growth, curtails economic productivity, and poses challenges to energy sustainability in households and increases overreliance on fuel for energy production in several African homes. Overall, according to Mo Ibrahim Foundation, 2022, electricity shortages cost Africa up to 4% of its GDP per year.
The Lighting an African Family (LAAF): Improving access to clean energy and environmental sustainability in Africa project, will aim to support the increase in access to clean energy for urban communities in select cities in Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria though advocacy and knowledge sharing activities on clean energy with key stakeholders, and establishing the existing gaps in accessing cleaner forms of energy at the end user levels. This will inform the project outputs both at the regional and country levels. Project Approach
To deliver on the project objectives and achieve its desired impacts at the city, national and regional level, the project will deploy a series of activities, complemented with a communication/visibility plan to amplify awareness on the importance of clean energy. The following outputs will aim to deliver the project objective and the outcomes;
Output 1: Development of an evidence-based assessment of access to clean energy in Africa
The starting point of the delivery of the project will be the delivery of an evidence-based knowledge product on the state of access to clean energy at the local and national levels. The evidence based assessment will highlight key indicators on the level of clean energy at the National and at the city level, using a targeted community within the urban area as a case study. The indicators that the assessment will target to highlight will be the level of access to both on-grid and off-grid energy supply at the national level, and at the city level i.e end user level. The data will also highlight the gaps in the supply of clean energy and capacity needs by institutional stakeholders in the clean energy sector. At the end of the project, the project will have delivered one assessment report/ knowledge product on the level of access to clean energy in Africa with analysis and case studies from 4 countries and cities i.e Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Nigeria.
Output 2: Conduct advocacy and knowledge exchange activities aimed at improving access to clean energy in Africa.
The project will simultaneously conduct advocacy and knowledge sharing activities while developing the assessment reports, this will be achieved through conducting community and institutional stakeholders engagement activities with an aim of collecting data on access to clean energy and sensitizing the wider stakeholders on the need to use and promote the use of clean energy and environmentally friendly activities. In specific, the activities will be complemented with trainings on how to use and maintain solar energy equipment as one of the off grid clean energy sources and entrepreneurial skills for the youth involved in informal trade. Project implementation and Management
To achieve it’s objective in the four select countries and cities, the project will use an incremental approach in its implementation, it will strive to ensure lessons learnt from the project implementation from the previous city is applied in the next city and so on. This will improve efficiency in project deliverables and overall synergy with the project idea. The project will adopt the following steps: i. UN-Habitat and Shenzhen Poweroak Newener Company Limited, based in China with representation in Africa, based in Nairobi, Kenya will form a joint steering committee that will monitor the progress of the project implementation as well as provide suggestions and decisions in project implementation. The project will also form a technical team that comprises Country leads or Focal points and a regional coordinator that will aim to oversee the smooth implementation of the project activities. ii. Based on the implementation schedule, UN-Habitat will recruit a National urban basic service and/or urban energy personnel to document the gaps and needs for cleaner energy at city, national and regional levels. This will be done though desktop study and review, engagement with key stakeholders i.e community and institutional stakeholders at all relevant levels. This activity will be conducted through the below schedule; - a. The project will start off in Kenya, by analyzing of the level of access to clean energy at the National level, this will be done through desk top analysis and sourcing available research and published data on clean energy in Kenya.
